headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Uptrend intact, but momentum cooled after the $87K rejection

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The market remains in an early-stage uptrend, so the posture is still to increase acquisition spend, weighted toward active-trader and non-stablecoin channels that tend to benefit most in this phase. Signal confidence has, however, eased from high to medium (55/100) after a failed push above $87,000 shook out leveraged buyers, and the long-term average is still declining. That argues for scaling up in measured steps and keeping some budget in reserve rather than committing it all at once. This is a budget-posture view built on past data, not trading advice and not a forecast.

reasons: BTC is 19% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.19).
Momentum cooled to +0.31 (from +0.48) after the $87K rejection.
200-day average still falling (-4.2% over 90 days); breadth only 52%.
watch: The key tension is warm sentiment versus defensive positioning: Fear & Greed reads 65 (Greed) while funding has slid to a -1.82 z-score, and yesterday's push to about $87,187 ended with $433.57M of liquidations, three-quarters of them longs. Momentum has eased from +0.48 to +0.31 and signal confidence has dropped from high (70) to medium (55), while the 200-day average is still declining and breadth sits at 52%. Price holding the mid-$80,000s with funding normalising would steady the read; a slide toward the roughly $73,700 short-term-holder cost basis reported on 1 October, or renewed ETF outflows, would weaken it.
analysis: Short-term sentiment is neutral (-0.07 of a possible ±1): the crowd mood and actual positioning are pointing in opposite directions, and they roughly cancel out. Fear & Greed at 65 (Greed) is the warm side of the ledger, but perpetual funding has dropped to a -1.82 z-score, deeper than yesterday's -1.01, which means traders are paying to be short rather than chasing longs — that cuts against the greedy headline mood and keeps the score from leaning bullish. The latest 24 hours explain why: after the soft September jobs report (payrolls +29,000, unemployment 4.2%, per the BLS figures cited by crypto.news), BTC touched about $87,187 before a liquidation wave pushed it back to the mid-$84,000s, with CoinGlass recording $433.57M of crypto liquidations, 74% of them longs (Crypto Times, 3 Oct). Even after that flush, the market is not stressed: realised volatility sits at the 38th percentile of its two-year range, Bollinger width is 15.7%, DVOL is 35.5 and the VIX is a calm 15.3, reinforcing that this was a leverage reset rather than a panic. Open interest of about $8.3B and a long/short account ratio of 1.22 show retail accounts still tilted long even as funding says the larger money is net short, and the stablecoin supply ratio of 5.44 indicates sidelined stablecoin buying power is moderate rather than abundant. For this lean to turn bullish, funding would need to normalise back toward zero without the Greed reading tipping into extreme territory; a further slide in Fear & Greed alongside rising volatility would push it bearish.

Medium-term momentum is bullish-leaning (+0.31 of a possible ±1), though it has cooled noticeably from yesterday's +0.48 as price slipped back from its $87K high. The core supports are still in place: the 90-day rate of change is +33%, the 50-day average sits 10.5% above the 200-day (firmly on the golden-cross side) and weekly RSI at 60 is firm without being stretched, all reinforcing the bullish lean. What holds it back from strongly bullish is participation: only 52% of the last 90 days closed above the 200-day average, so the headline 33% gain has come from a relatively narrow run rather than a broad, sustained advance, and on-chain activity is slightly contracting versus its yearly average (active-address ratio 0.98), which cuts against the price signal. Bitcoin dominance at 58.6% shows capital is still concentrating in BTC rather than rotating into riskier altcoins, consistent with a cautious, BTC-led phase. US spot ETF flows add context rather than conviction: a nine-session inflow streak of roughly $3.08B ended with a net outflow of about $148.7M on 30 September (crypto.news), and the latest tracked day shows a modest +$31.7M inflow — positive, but a fraction of the streak's pace. The next FOMC meeting is on 27 October, a scheduled macro event inside this one-month window. Breadth pushing clearly above 55% would strengthen this lean; a weekly RSI drop below 50 or a run of ETF outflows would weaken it toward neutral.

Long-term trend is bullish-leaning (+0.27 of a possible ±1): price is above its key long-run averages, but the long-run averages themselves have not yet turned up. The Mayer Multiple of 1.19 puts BTC 19% above its 200-day average and the 200-week multiple of 1.28 places it mid-cycle, both reinforcing the bullish lean without signalling overheating. The main thing pulling against that read is direction: the 200-day average is still falling (-4.2% over 90 days), and price remains 32% below its all-time high, so this is a recovery inside a larger drawdown rather than a confirmed new cycle advance. Cycle-heat gauges agree there is no excess — the Puell Multiple at 0.99 shows normal miner economics and the Pi-Cycle gap of -54.8% is far from the zero line that has historically coincided with cycle tops (both context only, not scored). Structural demand remains a support: public companies now hold about 1.28M BTC and cumulative US spot ETF net inflows stand near $57.7B, and an SEC custody proposal reported on 2 October (Investing.com) is a regulatory development aimed at institutional participation. The macro backdrop cuts the other way: a 10-year Treasury yield of 5.28% and a 3.63% fed funds rate keep the cost of capital high for risk assets. The 200-day slope flattening and turning positive would strengthen this lean considerably; a sustained break back below the 200-day average would flip it toward neutral.

team_notes.marketing: Keep weighting active-trader and non-stablecoin channels, but lead messaging with the steady three-month trend (+33% over 90 days) and product reliability rather than breakout urgency — Friday's $87K spike reversed and flushed $434M of mostly long positions. With Fear & Greed at 65, funding negative and confidence now medium, keep stablecoin-first campaigns warm as a hedge rather than cutting them back.
